blocks.text: A software team wants research, approved email or LinkedIn outreach, reply triage and a sales-accepted handoff for one buyer segment. Sales owns expert questions and discovery. An agency proposal includes research and a manager but excludes data. An internal hiring plan includes a rep but leaves management and coverage unassigned. Neither scope is ready to compare until those blanks are resolved.

blocks.title: Normalize the work
rows: Targeting and claims
Name the approver and exception rule.
Allocate product and sales time to approvals.
Research and messages
Confirm data, tools and change ownership.
Assign the operator and manager. Include licenses.
Replies and discovery
Name daily reply coverage and sales handoff.
Name cover during absences. Allocate discovery.
Transfer or replacement
Specify exports, use rights and a receiving owner.
Budget recruiting, onboarding and backup.

sections.title: Compare time and costs on one horizon

blocks.text: The fictional agency brief needs two hours a week of client approvals and one hour of evidence review. The hiring brief needs those same three hours plus four hours of coaching and coverage. Over a 12-week planning window that is 36 versus 84 client hours, before one-off recruitment or transition. Verify availability and value the time consistently in the existing cost model. A blank supplier fee or hiring cost stays unknown.

Compare setup, recurring delivery, tools and staff time separately. Date the start of usable work and separate training or setup from operation. A short window can favour a fast launch even if a longer window favours internal capability. Recalculate at 3, 6 and 12 months when you have verified inputs. Do not compare a complete managed programme with a salary alone.

blocks.title: Decision examples
rows: Valid offer, no daily operator
Scope managed execution with named client and sales owners.
Hire once repeatability and coaching capacity are demonstrated.
Stable process, internal manager available
Build in-house and protect the manager’s time.
Use temporary cover if recruitment slips and the launch still matters.
Demand uncertain, possible operator later
Test a bounded segment and decide how learning will transfer.
Delay expansion if fit or sales follow-up is unresolved.
Nobody owns discovery
Defer both purchases and assign a sales owner.
Reopen after that person accepts the handoff and can cover replies.

blocks.title: Decision record
rows: Chosen scope
Managed research and outreach for one segment. Client owns approvals, technical replies and discovery.
Open items
Tool costs and backup for reply escalation. Obtain written scope and owner acceptance before launch.
Transfer proof
The receiver can reconstruct one research record, act on a reply and honor a stop request with the proper access and rights.
Reconsider
If the receiver cannot handle an exception or the export omits the suppression state, keep the current operator and repeat the test.

blocks.text: Check the first real buying decision against the record. Keep revenue, pipeline and profit separate. A forecast with unverified conversion or margin cannot settle the operating choice.

answer: Choose an agency when the missing work is recurring execution and you can still provide decisions, approvals and sales follow-up. Build in-house when the work is repeatable, strategically important and you can recruit and manage it. Compare the same scope over the same period, including client time, ramp and exit.
